subject: Request: Exec approval — Heliomed private install terms & concession for EU-residency
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@heliomed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private install proposal + audit window — initial SOW and redlines attached

Eleanor —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is the latest SOW and our proposed redline that captures the private (on-prem) deployment architecture, KMS/HSM integration notes, and the runbook access profile you asked for. Key customer asks summarized below: 

- EU-only data residency in customer-controlled VLANs (Heliomed-managed datacenter)
- Annual compliance audit with 48-hour timeboxed engineer access to logs and runbook read-only snapshots
- 90-day forensic window (retain request/trace logs for 90 days on your enclave)
- No remote egress of customer data; exception for telemetry summarized states only aggregated metrics will leave the enclave
- HSM integration for key material and optional customer-side KMS
- Commercial concession: 30% one-time implementation credit + 6-month pilot rate at reduced price

We flagged a few non-standard contract points in the redline (see Helio_Redline_v4.pdf): limited audit scope, runbook masking, and indemnity carveouts. These will need an exec signoff on the commercial concession and a legal confirmation on the audit scope.

Next steps I propose: if internal OK, I can send an approval note to legal/execs and follow-up with a DocuSign binder.

Thanks —
Lukas Meyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Helimed_Redline_v4.pdf (redline), SOW_OnPrem_v2.docx (SOW)
From: Eleanor Briggs <eleanor.briggs@heliomed.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private install proposal + audit window — initial SOW and redlines attached

Lukas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clear summary. A few clarifications from our security and procurement teams: 

1) Audit access: we need ability to validate control implementation during an annual compliance test. We expect read-only log access for up to 72 hours for our auditors and a 7-day window for remediation evidence collection. Can Redwood accept a timeboxed 72-hour access once per year (not continuous)?

2) Forensic window: 90 days is acceptable but we need a signed commitment that data will be retained and that snapshots can be provided for specific tickets.

3) Implementation credit: the 30% implementation credit is material for our approval. Can you confirm this will be applied as an upfront credit on the invoice schedule?

We prefer to close the commercial and security points in this week’s executive review.

Best,
Eleanor Briggs
Head of Procurement, Heliomed Corp
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Helio asks — exec approval request (commercial + audit scope)

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Helio's note. The ask coming from procurement/security is: 72-hour timeboxed auditor access once annually (Heliomed's auditors), a contractual 90-day forensic retention and an upfront 30% implementation credit applied against invoice schedule.

Redline has two legal asks: (a) limit audit scope to logs/runbook snapshots and not live system configs; (b) runbook content must be masked for internal IP. Aditya please confirm the HSM/KMS approach and whether we can guarantee no remote egress and the snapshot capabilities to fulfill the 90-day retention.

Karthik — need an exec-level decision on the 30% credit and whether we can offer the timeboxed 72-hour auditor window as phrased (legal will prefer more constraints). If we can do this I will propose we close with a pilot at reduced monthly rates for the first 6 months.

Thanks —
Lukas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio asks — exec approval request (commercial + audit scope)

Team —

High level: I support moving forward with a concession but with guardrails. Proposed decisions: 

- Commercial: approve a one-time 25% implementation credit (not 30%) applied as a credit against the first invoice milestone. Rationale: preserves margin and is easier to justify to finance.
- Pilot pricing: approve 6-month pilot at 15% off published rate (we can convert to standard rate after pilot).
- Audit: approve timeboxed auditor access once per year for up to 48 hours (not 72) — with strict pre-approved test plan and access request process; legal must sign an audit protocol addendum that limits queries and prohibits persistent remote tooling.
- Forensic retention: commit to 90-day retention for request/trace logs on their enclave; require explicit Data Retention SLA and notice period for snapshot exports.

Lauren / Legal: can you draft a short Audit Protocol Addendum that limits scope to read-only artifacts, requires 72-hour notice for any access, and disallows live-system manipulations? We should push for 48 hours operational access but allow the 72-hour evidence-collection exception in the protocol for specific cases (requires pre-approval).

Aditya: confirm HSM/KMS integration feasibility and whether we can guarantee that no plaintext egress will leave the enclave. If any telemetry needs to flow out, it must be anonymized and aggregated only.

If we agree, Lukas will communicate the final concessions back to Heliomed and prep the DocuSign bundle.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio asks — exec approval request (commercial + audit scope)

Confirmed from infra: HSM/KMS integration is feasible in their environment. Notes:

- We can operate with customer-managed HSMs and use Redwoods connectors to store only wrapped keys inside the enclave. No plaintext keys will leave the customer VLAN.
- For the auditor access: we can produce read-only log snapshots and mask sensitive fields. Providing a 72-hour evidence-collection window is operationally heavy; recommend 48 hours by default and a documented exception process for 72-hour evidence pulls (requires legal sign-off and an ops runbook).
- Forensic retention of 90 days for request/trace logs is feasible; we will document retention SLAs and snapshot export procedures.
- Telemetry: we will only surface aggregated metrics off the enclave; nothing PII or request-level will egress.

I will work with Lauren to detail the access controls in the Audit Protocol Addendum.

- Aditya

Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final concessions and next steps — Heliomed Private Install

Eleanor / Peter —

Thanks for your patience while we lined up internal approvals. Per internal review we can commit to the following final concessions: 

1) Commercial: 25% one-time implementation credit applied to the first invoice milestone; 6-month pilot pricing at 15% off published rate.
2) Audit: one annual auditor access event up to a default 48-hour operational window for read-only log/runbook snapshots. We will include an Audit Protocol Addendum that: requires a pre-approved test plan, 72-hour notice for special evidence requests, and forbids live system manipulation or persistent tooling.
3) Forensic retention: 90 days for request/trace logs stored on the customer enclave; we will provide snapshot exports per the Data Retention SLA.
4) HSM/KMS: we will support customer-managed HSMs; no plaintext key egress; telemetry will be anonymized and aggregated only.

Next steps: Lauren will circulate the Audit Protocol Addendum and the updated SOW redline. We will package the concession as an addendum and a DocuSign binder. Please confirm you are aligned with these points and we'll send the DocuSign link for signatures.

Warm regards,
Lukas Meyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
